verdicts.reason: A reads properly as a banner: phone, then the two-line headline and subtext, then the orange CTA on the right. It has two flaws: the subtext is nearly as large as the headline, which weakens the hierarchy, and the tiny phone is crammed against the left edge. B puts the 'Try It Free' CTA first at the far left, so the action comes before the message, which breaks the reading order. B also squeezes the phone mockup into a sliver against the right edge, where it can't be recognised, and the CTA text is very small.
